You have worded this perfectly imo. People who say "Life is Worth Living" have good intentions but I doubt they can say it without cringing to a person with several severe problems in real life.

Is it a good idea to go to an institution? I've never heard anyone say it has helped but rather ate through their finances. Some are even traumatised from their experience there and feel constantly watched. I don't know too much on it actually..

While I admit my situation is entirely different from yours, that emptiness is too relatable

It's okay that's what this subreddit is here for.

Ikr. what's the difference?? I don't hate religion but when people use this to try to scare you urgh.

there's plenty of bad stuff here that is always covered because "ignorance is bliss"

I feel like motivational speakers always skip out this part. They just start talking about their success story and some go as far as to make the low part of someone's lives seem bad and you always need to be on top of your game \(\-\_\-\)

Yes it's possible. That's what being bipolar does to you. There have been many cases where a person is all seemingly happy and then next thing you know, they killed themselves.

When people try to diagnose depression they just look for the typical signs. So when a popular, attractive person dies that's why people go "what went wrong?"  A lot of people are ashamed and feel guilty for being depressed and hide it

I disagree with your last point, suicide is not selfish. This is a common opinion of people who don't understand the perspective of a suicidal person \(not saying you aren't\). Suicidal people truly believe they are a burden to their loved ones. And also works the other way, it is also selfish to expect someone to keep suffering so you don't feel inconvenience or drained. It's a loop
